title: Micro-shield rollout guardrails and retro template
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch for a small/fast production rollout pattern were calling "micro-shield". Goal is to give small feature launches an automated, low-touch safety net: fast canary + automated throttles + ephemeral "shield" capacity that absorbs outage/throttle events and prevents customer-visible errors during traffic shocks. This doc bundles the operator checklist, a 3-day rollout calendar, signal matrix (triggers -> actions), a Slack comms snippet, a short release-notes draft, and a retro template to capture lessons quickly.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: release engineers, on-call SREs, primary feature owner, product manager.
- Scope: launches that change model routing, egress policies, or introduce new heavy CPU/GPU paths. Not intended for infra upgrades or database schema changes.

Quick TL;DR:
- Launch window: 09:00-13:00 PT (16:00-20:00 UTC) to coincide with lower APAC traffic.
- 4-phase rollout: 0.5% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% (with automated hold/failover at each gate).
- Safety components: shield nodes (ephemeral capacity), traffic cork (rate limiter), emergency reroute to fallback model variant.

Preflight checklist (48-24h):
- [ ] Postmortem review: scan last 3 similar rollouts for recurring failure modes. Link: confluence:release-orbit-2027/lessons
- [ ] Canary config in feature flagging tool verified (rules + percentiles). Ticket: JIRA-RELEASE-1482
- [ ] Shield pool capacity provisioned and smoke-tested (SRE switchover script tested).
- [ ] Observability: dashboards for latency, p50/p95/p99, error rate (4xx/5xx), token-rate, GPU memory pressure, KV cache-hit ratio.
- [ ] Tracing: distributed traces annotated with release tag and route id.
- [ ] Rollback playbook present and validated with dry-run (rollback route, feature flag off, shield drain).
- [ ] Pager/rotation assigned and shared in the Slack channel.

Day-of timeline (short window):
- T-60m: Final go/no-go meeting (owner, SRE, release eng, PM). Verify smoke scripts green.
- T-30m: Provision shield nodes if not persistent; warm caches with synthetic prefixes.
- T-15m: Baseline telemetry snapshot captured (save dashboard links).
- T0 (09:00 PT): Activate feature flag at 0.5% traffic. Start 15m steady watch.
- Gate 1: If no triggers fired in 15m, increase to 5% and watch 20m.
- Gate 2: If steady, increase to 25% and watch 30m. Bring capacity to handle additional 2x token-rate.
- Gate 3: If steady, expand to 100% with staggered 15m micro-bumps (25%->50%->75%->100%).
- Post-100%: Maintain heightened watch for 60m, then normal monitoring.

Signal matrix (metric -> threshold -> immediate action):
- Error rate (5xx) absolute > 0.5% for 5m -> ACTION: hold rollout, engage shield reroute, page SRE P1 channel.
- Latency p99 increases > 2x baseline for 10m -> ACTION: reduce rollout by 50% of current percent, enable cache bypass metric collection, run heap/GC snapshot if applicable.
- GPU memory pressure > 85% sustained 5m -> ACTION: divert traffic to fallback quantized model, spin additional shield nodes if autoscale fails.
- Token throughput drop (unexpected) > 20% vs baseline -> ACTION: check upstream rate-limiters, circuit-breaker logs; if unknown cause, hold and escalate.
- Function-call failures (e.g., tool-calls) > 0.2% -> ACTION: fail traffic for that route to helper model and annotate telemetry.

Automated controls and playbooks:
- Traffic cork: an automated rate limiter that reduces new sessions if error signals exceed thresholds. Config: 10s cooldown, stepdown 50%.
- Shield drain: when switching off shield nodes, do a 90s graceful drain, copy KV-cache prefixes back to main cache (if applicable), and run 2 quick requests to ensure warm state.
- Fallback routing: deploy rule that switches to quantized or distilled model variant on capacity/latency triggers. Rule order: explicit route -> canary -> fallback.

Comms snippets (Slack, use #release-orbit channel and @oncall):
- Preflight (T-60m): "T-60: micro-shield rollout for feature X. Oncall: @andre, SRE lead: @maya. Smoke OK. Shield nodes provisioned. Will start 09:00 PT. Link dashboards: <dash-url>"
- Gate hold: "HOLD at 5%: p99 latency +120% vs baseline over 20m. Holding and investigating (owner: @sofia). Paging SRE. See trace: <trace-url>"
- Rollforward complete: "Rollout to 100% complete at 11:05 PT. Post-watch for 60m. Postmortem link placeholder: <postmortem-draft>"

Release notes (draft) - concise for product/marketing / changelog:
- Feature: Model routing for "safety-filter" enabled on the default route. Improves prompt filtering latency by using a distilled filter model in low-risk queries.
- Performance: Improved cold-start handling for KV cache by prewarming shield pool during rollout. Expected to reduce cold latencies for first-token by ~12%.
- Fixes: Addressed an intermittent egress timeout when calling external tool X under high token-rate.
- Known issues: On very long-context prompts (>12k tokens), the fallback quantized model may produce lower quality; automatic rollback triggers will engage in that case.

Quick rollback decision tree (operator checklist):
- If hold persists > 30m with unresolved cause -> rollback to previous route and disable feature flag; notify product and customers if any SLO breach.
- If shield nodes show repeated OOMs -> emergency rollback and create high-priority Jira bug.
- If spike is localized to one region -> restrict rollout to impacted regions and continue progressive rollout elsewhere.

Post-release retro template (capture within 24-72h):
- Summary: one-paragraph summary (who, what, when).
- What went well: bullet list.
- What surprised us: bullet list.
- Timeline of decisions: 6-10 bullets with timestamps.
- Signal false-positives: any metric alerts that were noise and why.
- Action items: owner + ETA for each (e.g., fix alert threshold, improve dashboard, add synthetic test).
- Customer impact notes: list customers/segments affected and mitigation performed.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q: Should shields be always-on for heavy-model routes or only provisioned per-release? Tradeoff: cost vs. reliability.
- TODO: Add a synthetic load generator job for the quantized fallback variant so we can profile memory/cold-start before rollout. (owner: Ethan)
- TODO: Add an automatic post-rollout quality-eval run (against golden prompts) to detect silent regressions within 2h of 100% roll. (owner: Maya)

Appendix - quick commands / links:
- Shield provision CLI: ./infra/shieldctl provision --pool micro-shield-1 --size 3
- Drain shield: ./infra/shieldctl drain --pool micro-shield-1 --grace 90
- Emergency rollback (feature flag): flags.redwood.com/featureX -> toggle OFF
- Dashboards: <latency-dash> | <errors-dash> | <gpu-ops-dash>

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep the initial canary tiny for this feature because it touches model selection logic.
- Consider adding a small A/B quality eval in Gate 2 to ensure fallback hasn't regressed user-visible scores.
- Remember to tag all traces and spans with release_tag=micro-shield-2027-03 so filtering is trivial.

Document history:
- 2027-03-09: Sofia initial draft
- 2027-03-11: Added automated controls section (Andre)
- 2027-03-12: Updated signal thresholds after SRE dry-run (Maya)

End of doc.
